segments.text: Welcome to the Robotics News Digest for November 2nd, 2026.
We've got big updates, including rising North American orders, advancements in autonomous driving, and robot challenges.
Tune in for your daily dose of robotics.
From Robotics & Automation News, North American robot orders increased by twenty-five percent in the third quarter of 2026.
This report details the significant growth observed in robot procurement across North American companies during that period.

North American companies ordered ten thousand nine hundred eighty-nine robots valued at seven hundred twenty-three point five million dollars, representing a twenty-five percent increase in both units and total value compared to the prior year.
This expansion was fueled by robust demand within several key sectors, specifically Automotive Original Equipment Manufacturers, Semiconductors and Electronics, and Life Sciences.
Furthermore, orders for collaborative robots experienced a substantial fifty-six percent increase during the same quarter.
This data indicates a broad and intensifying market for robotics across diverse industrial applications.
Positive momentum is entering the final quarter of 2026 for the sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, BMW and Embotech move one million vehicles using automated driving technology.
This achievement demonstrates the scalability of Automated Driving In-Plant within the BMW Group's production network.
The deployment involved moving one million vehicles across four production sites located in the United Kingdom and Germany.
This operation supports approximately three thousand five hundred vehicle movements daily with a reported availability exceeding ninety-nine point five percent.

Embotech supplied the necessary AI-based software and safety architecture for this reliable operation, showcasing how the technology enhances production efficiency, flexibility, and safety across the network.
This deployment indicates a significant step forward for the integration of automated driving systems into large-scale manufacturing processes.
From Humanoids Daily, "AGIBOT Livestreams Six G2 Robots in a 24-Hour Convenience Store Challenge".
This report details a twenty-four hour challenge where six AGIBOT G2 robots operated within a convenience store environment.

The challenge, conducted between November second and third, required the robots to perform tasks including stocking shelves, preparing coffee, and engaging with customers during peak operational times.
The livestream provided an extended view of the robots managing routine variations and interruptions inherent in continuous work within a dynamic human setting.
Assessment of task success and autonomy focused on the robots' intervention and recovery procedures throughout the event.
This experiment offers data on robotic adaptability in complex, real-world commercial settings.
Further observation of these systems will inform future developments in autonomous service technology.
From Robotics & Automation News, "What battery technology will power the next generation of humanoid robots?".
This report examines the battery technologies poised to power future humanoid robots, focusing on advancements in energy density, safety, and longevity.
Current humanoid robots predominantly utilize NMC-based lithium-ion batteries, which currently balance energy density requirements with operational performance criteria.
Future research is focusing heavily on solid-state batteries, which promise increased energy density and enhanced safety through the elimination of liquid electrolytes.
Alternatively, lithium-sulfur cells are being explored for their high theoretical energy density, although challenges remain regarding cycle life and charging speeds.
Furthermore, adjustments to NMC cathode compositions, specifically increasing nickel content, offer a pathway to improve performance while mitigating cobalt usage.
The progression toward these advanced battery systems is necessitated by the demand for greater energy density and improved safety in humanoid applications.
This transition signals a necessary technological shift in energy storage for the advancement of humanoid robotics.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Interview with TorqueAGI founder: ‘Most robot AI is a language or vision model with robot data added to it’".
This segment reports on TorqueAGI's development of a World-Reasoning Model for industrial robots and heavy machinery, which incorporates physics and geometry into a spatio-temporal architecture.
The model allows machines to adapt to changes and learn new tasks from minimal demonstrations using existing operational data.
This approach differs from vision-language-action models by building reasoning directly on spatial-temporal graphs instead of solely relying on large demonstration sets.
The Sovereign Physical AI architecture mandates local model execution for operational autonomy and accountability for industrial equipment.
This advancement signals a shift toward physically grounded reasoning in robotics.
From The Robot Report, "Solving the Interconnect Challenge in Modern Robotics: How 3M Is Engineering for Motion, Density, and Uptime".

This story details how 3M addresses challenges in robotics interconnects related to signal integrity, mechanical durability, and board space through specific engineering solutions. 3M’s portfolio addresses these issues with high-flex cable assemblies possessing validated cycle life, fast IDC termination methods, and reduced-pitch connectors designed to conserve board space.
Additionally, the company provides solutions that enhance reliability against vibration and manage electromagnetic interference and crosstalk within dense wiring configurations.
These interconnect strategies offer engineers validated options to improve the reliability and performance of next-generation robotic hardware.
This work provides validated pathways for advancing the performance and dependability of future robotic systems.
From Humanoids Daily, "DEEP Robotics Humanoids Join Traffic Police at Hangzhou Marathon".
This report details the deployment of DEEP Robotics humanoids in traffic management at the Hangzhou Marathon, demonstrating their capability in performing specific support tasks.
The robots, designated Hangxing No.2, utilized the DR02 platform to assist with traffic management duties around the Huanglong Sports Center.
These units executed patrols, issued safety warnings, and handled public inquiries, employing standardized traffic gestures and broadcasting safety advisories to support roadside operations.
The deployment served as an opportunity to test a repeatable model for humanoid support amidst dynamic crowd and vehicle patterns.
The actual efficacy of this system is contingent upon consistent performance and clearly defined roles between the robots and human officers.
The event suggests advancements in applying humanoid technology for real-time public safety coordination.
From Humanoid.guide, Meta reportedly builds Max humanoid prototype with Fourier.

This report details the development of a humanoid prototype named Max in collaboration with the Chinese robotics company Fourier, which serves as a physical embodiment of Meta’s Muse agent focusing on household tasks.
The prototype was developed in approximately three months and weighs around one hundred six pounds or forty-eight kilograms.
This development involved leveraging Fourier's expertise in robotics hardware to support Meta's ongoing AI and software advancements.
Meta intends to construct a second version of the robot, but there are no plans for commercial sales, indicating its role as an internal development platform supported by the partnership.
The collaboration signals continued integration between advanced AI software and physical robotics hardware in the technology sector.
From Humanoid.guide, RoboParty launches RP1 humanoid with open hardware and software.
This report details the introduction of an open hardware and software research platform designed for advancing research in embodied artificial intelligence.

The platform features a humanoid robot with twenty-four or thirty actuated degrees of freedom, providing researchers with full access to mechanical designs, actuators, firmware, control algorithms, and learning tools.
This open approach enables teams to modify the robot for research into gait, balance control, and embodied AI through simulation and physical deployment.

The system includes built-in capabilities for walking, fall recovery, and motion tracking, supplemented by tools such as VR teleoperation, allowing for practical debugging advantages across all components.
This development signals a new methodology for exploring complex robotic behaviors in research settings.
From Humanoids Daily, "1X Teammates Use Spare NEO Heads to Test Home Integrations, Starting With the TV".

This report details how 1X teammates are utilizing spare NEO heads to test home integrations, demonstrating the potential for home robots to understand spoken requests and act across household devices.

The demonstration involved a NEO head responding to a spoken request by selecting and starting a film on a television, showcasing an informal setup for testing command recognition and cross-device operation.

This specific interaction illustrates the potential for a home robot to interpret commands and execute actions within a domestic environment, although the demonstration does not detail the underlying technology or an imminent commercial release.
The company continues to await customer deliveries for the NEO robots, which are currently targeted for 2026.
This activity indicates ongoing development in practical home automation capabilities for future robotic systems.
From Robotics & Automation News, Agility Robotics says more than 30 companies are considering the Digit humanoid robot.
This report details the expansion of commercial use for the Digit robot through new agreements and customer programs.

Agility Robotics has established a commercial agreement with GXO and is conducting paid programs with manufacturing customers, resulting in over thirty prospective customers across sectors like automotive and logistics.
Operations at forthcoming GXO facilities are scheduled for early 2027 utilizing Digit 4, with a transition planned to Digit 5 later.
Agility is also developing Digit 5, intended for broader industrial workflows, which is anticipated to be generally available in late 2027.
The company is advancing commercialization through customer demonstrations and a cloud-based fleet management platform.
This progression indicates increasing industry interest in humanoid robotics for industrial applications.
From Humanoids Daily, Lightberry’s Lumi Gains Conditional FCC Covered List Exemption.
This report details how Lightberry has secured a conditional exemption from the FCC Covered List to facilitate manufacturing relocation to the United States.
The approval permits Lightberry to pursue independent FCC certification prior to offering the robots to customers.
This exemption is conditional upon strict adherence to the onshoring plan and continuous product vetting, with provisions for potential withdrawal of the approval.
Lightberry intends to commence domestic production utilizing the robot's body, head, and hands.
Achieving independent certification precedes the possibility of off-the-shelf sales.
This development indicates a pathway for advanced robotics technology to be manufactured within the United States.
Further developments in independent certification processes will be observed within the technology sector.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, CR Hand!".

This report details the introduction of the CR Hand, a compact robotic hand from Curious Robotics, which serves as a platform for examining the balance between dexterity, strength, weight, and cost in robotic hand design.
The device is constructed from FDM printed plastic and incorporates integrated servo motors and a controller, with a retail price of one thousand five hundred United States dollars.
Assessments indicate the hand achieved a Humanoid.Guide Hand Score of three out of ten, reflecting developing dexterity and lower strength in its current configuration.
The design emphasizes an affordable and practical approach suitable for educational applications and research.
This development highlights ongoing research into optimizing the physical parameters of robotic manipulation systems for practical implementation.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Elf Xuan 2.0!".
This report details the development of an upper body humanoid prototype focused on expressive interaction and stationary public presentation.
The Elf Xuan 2.0 is an upper body humanoid developed by AheadForm featuring an elven design with lifelike silicone skin and articulated arms.
It incorporates a movable waist and sophisticated facial expressions achieved through brushless micro motors for movement.

Measuring one hundred sixty-five centimeters in height and weighing fifty kilograms, the robot is designed for expressive interaction rather than broad physical capability, and the prototype is currently priced at fifty-five thousand US dollars.
This development emphasizes visual presentation over advanced physical autonomy in current robotic systems.
The ongoing progression of such expressive robotics signals a continued focus on sophisticated human-robot interface design.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, YMBot D4!".

This segment details the introduction of the YMBot D4, an industrial mobile humanoid robot designed for factory and logistics environments, with a recorded skill score indicating its development level is in the developing category.

The YMBot D4 features a humanoid upper body mounted on a folding wheeled chassis, equipped with two articulated arms featuring five-fingered hands for sorting and assembly tasks, and incorporates obstacle avoidance for navigation.
Standing at 165 centimeters and weighing 100 kilograms, the robot has a maximum speed of 5.4 kilometers per hour and a strength capacity of 10 kilograms.
Communication with the robot is facilitated through ROS 2, and the unit is currently available as a prototype with a listed price of fifty-five thousand United States dollars.
The introduction of such specialized mobile robotics signals continued advancement in practical industrial automation and humanoid engineering.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Billi!".

This segment details the introduction of Billi, a wheeled, hybrid humanoid robot developed by NEUBILITY for industrial logistics and material handling, with performance ratings indicating an early stage for general-purpose systems.
The robot incorporates a mobile base, a humanlike upper body, and two arms equipped with five-fingered hands, allowing for a rotating and adjustable upper body.
It possesses a maximum speed of six kilometers per hour and weighs one hundred and ten kilograms.
Navigation and obstacle avoidance are achieved through camera-based perception, and the system's navigation and manipulation capabilities are rated at one out of five.
Billi functions as an early prototype emphasizing a mobile platform for sorting and navigation within industrial environments.
This development signals continued progression in the application of mobile robotics within logistics and material handling sectors.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, YMBot C!".
This segment reports on the development and current status of the YMBot C, a full-size bipedal humanoid robot.
The robot measures one hundred seventy-four centimeters in height and weighs seventy-five kilograms.

The development was carried out by Jiangsu Yunmu Intelligent Manufacturing Technology Co., Ltd., with the design focused on cultural tourism and exhibitions, featuring a humanlike exterior with two arms and hands.
Confirmed capabilities for the prototype include obstacle avoidance for navigation, though scores for overall skill, navigation, and manipulation are currently low.
The robot remains in prototype form with a listed price of sixty thousand US dollars.
Further developments in humanoid robotics will indicate future advancements in embodied artificial intelligence.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, RealBot 01!".
This report details the specifications and capabilities of the RealBot 01, a wheeled humanoid robot developed by RealMan Robotics.
The robot measures one hundred sixty-eight centimeters tall and weighs one hundred twenty-five kilograms, demonstrating a top speed of five point four kilometers per hour.
It is equipped with two articulated arms capable of handling a combined payload of ten kilograms and possesses a four-hour operational runtime per charge.
The platform is modular, integrating with other systems and running on the Ubuntu 22.04 LTS operating system with ROS 2 Humble.
Documented functions include obstacle avoidance, goods sorting, and product assembly, emphasizing combined navigation and manipulation capabilities.
This development signals progress in embodied artificial intelligence and industrial automation sectors.
From The Robot Report, "Why physical AI is the next lucrative frontier".
This report examines the emergence of physical artificial intelligence as the next lucrative frontier, noting its rapid growth evidenced by record funding in robotics and autonomous systems.
Physical AI systems operate by perceiving environments, making real-time decisions, and adapting through real-world interaction.
This advancement is fueled by maturing technologies such as multimodal sensing, edge computing, and robotics foundation models.
This sector is poised for significant disruption across manufacturing, logistics, and other industries through the application of these integrated systems.
The development leverages advanced machine learning to enable physical agents to execute complex tasks autonomously in dynamic settings.
This progression signals a major shift toward embodied intelligence driving industrial automation and operational efficiency.
And that’s all the circuits we have for today.
Hope your algorithms are running smoothly.
Until tomorrow, keep building amazing things!
Peace out.
